title: 50 Cent Fires Back at T.I. in New ‘Power Origins’ Theme Song With Leon Thomas: Listen
summary: This feud ain't over just yet.
contentText:
After being on the receiving end of a handful of diss tracks from T.I. and his sons, it didn’t appear that 50 Cent planned to respond by stepping into the booth. That changed on Friday (March 6), when the G-Unit mogul responded to Tip with the Power Origins theme song.

Related

A Timeline of 50 Cent & T.I.’s Relationship

T.I. Talks Final Album, 50 Cent Feud, Status of ‘ATL 2’ & ‘Humbling’ Success of ‘LET EM KNOW’

T.I. Says He Didn’t ‘Enjoy’ His Kids Joining 50 Cent Beef, Admits Son King Crossed the Line

“They are gonna learn to leave me alone,” 50 captioned an X post alongside the release of “No One Told Us What We’re Here For” featuring Leon Thomas.

50 appears to direct a few bars at T.I. and his wife, Tiny Harris, while also speaking to their children. “I’m back on my dope boy grammar/ Your daddy made your mama eat every box in Atlanta/ Freak s—t, peep s—t/ Keep s—t, on the low/ But everybody know,” he raps with a reference to the sexual assault allegations Tip and Tiny faced.

The feud doesn’t appear to be anywhere close to over just yet. Fans gave 50 kudos for responding through a theme song for one of his shows, rather than a traditional diss track, which could prove to be a shrewd business move.

“Most men write a diss to get a reaction; 50 composes a theme to get a residual,” one fan wrote on X. “He is making you listen to his victory every time you press play. It is not just a song; it is a tax on T.I.’s sanity that collects interest every episode.”

However, T.I. doesn’t look to be too worried about 50’s response, as he dared the G-Unit mogul to reply by taunting him on Instagram.

“Drop whatever you choose,just please keep showing da world You a Ho!!! #OnClay & You still ain’t Tell us why you in 4K ‘D—k Pulling’ wit the smile of a Sissy????Pandora’s box is ajar sir… Good Luck FN You s—k,” T.I. wrote shortly after the song’s arrival.

Before 50 dropped “No One Told Us,” the trap pioneer wrote in a separate IG post: “We can go bar for bar, hit for hit, or doc for doc… either way all you gon do is show how much of a FN u is…. Let’s play. Nobody fears you over here Boo Boo.”

The T.I.-50 Cent beef became a family affair when Tip’s kids Domani and King Harris unleashed explosive disses against Fif. King unleashed another diss track on Friday (March 6) targeting the Queens icon, titled “Droptop.”

T.I. and 50’s feud was reignited in February when the Atlanta rapper blasted the “In Da Club” rapper for ducking him in a Verzuz battle. 50 trolled Tip and his family members on social media, which raised tensions, and T.I. headed to the booth to respond with four diss tracks.
